title: Dizzy Green and others who passed for white
summary: He tells how his school friend Orville Green went to Hollywood and passed for white, snubbing a friend, and mentions Willie Smith who could have passed.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, a lot of times that happened, you know, people didn't want to -- I know a fella that -- one of the first fellas when I was in school. His name was Dizzy Green, and Orville Green was his real name and his folks just looked like they were white, you know, and he looked white, see? But for some reason, they were colored, you know? And so he and I -- he used to fool around on the guitar and I'd fool around on the piano, you know what I mean, and so he left Muskogee and went to the coast, West Coast, because he wanted to better himself, I'm sure. So after he went to the West Coast, then I ran into a bunch of fellows that used to hang around us all the time and the first thing when I got to California, they told me, they says, 'Man, if you see Orville Green, don't say anything to him, man, because the cat going to sure make you feel bad.' I says, 'What do you mean?' And so this guy told me, he says, 'Well, man, you see, when I was out there in Hollywood,' he says, 'and I happened to look, see four or five guys talking, and I recognized Orville Green. I ran over there and says, 'Hi there, Orville. How you doing, man?' So Orville says, 'Well, hello there. Listen here, I'll tell you what you do. I'm real
busy right now. But come on by the house. I'm sure my mother or aunt will have some work for you to do. Come on by there any time."

And this guy really got angry at Orville. He got angry because he said, "Look, that guy had the nerve to pull that on me," you know? But you see, Orville had something else in mind. He had one thing in mind and he felt like that he didn't want to hurt his chances out there in Hollywood because this guy's knowing him because they say, "Hey, man, who's that? What do you know about this guy?" You know what I mean. And so consequently he set it all in front right away.
But you know, the opposite of that was Willie Smith with Lunceford.
I mean, he looked as white as anybody.
Willie could have passed anytime he got ready, but he never did.
Well, it's stupid really, any way you look at it.
